intended_object: The controlled unitary ∑_ω |ω⟩⟨ω| ⊗ (⊗_{i∈ι} U_{ω,i}) acting on ℂ^Ω ⊗ (ℂ^β)^{⊗ι}: conditioned on a classical/coherent control value ω, apply the tensor product of local unitaries U_{ω,i}. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the constituent definitions.
explanation: The definition is the block-diagonal matrix (Matrix.blockDiagonal' via coherentSharedRandomControlledUnitary) indexed by Σ ω, (ι → β). Each block is finiteTensorLocalUnitary (U ω), whose (q, r) entry is ∏_i U_{ω,i}(q i, r i), i.e. exactly the Kronecker/tensor product ⊗_i U_{ω,i} in the product basis. A block-diagonal matrix with blocks V_ω is precisely ∑_ω |ω⟩⟨ω| ⊗ V_ω, so this is the intended controlled tensor-product unitary, and it is correctly packaged as an element of the unitary group. Working over ℂ with finite index types is the natural setting for quantum unitaries. Every tensor factor uses the same local dimension β, which is standard for parallel repetition. Mathlib has no finite-family Kronecker product of matrices and no controlled unitary to cite as a counterpart.
